## Context

GitHub code scanning (CodeQL) reports 5 open findings, all rule
`py/clear-text-logging-sensitive-data`, operator-directed into the bug bash 2026-08-12.
Locations re-confirmed on CURRENT `origin/main` (line numbers below are exact as of the
tip; they match the scan's most recent instance):

- alert 83 — `src/rebar/_commands/__init__.py:199` — `print(f"Error: unknown leaf-write command '{command}'", ...)`
- alert 84 — `src/rebar/_commands/__init__.py:204` — `print(_usage_error(command, entry, "...unrecognised option '{offending}'..."))`
- alert 85 — `src/rebar/_commands/__init__.py:221` — `print(_usage_error(command, entry, "...refusing to drop {positionals[limit:]}..."))`
- alert 86 — `src/rebar/_commands/_seam.py:452` — `", ".join(data["secret_override"]["families"])` in `screen_event`
- alert 87 — `src/rebar/_commands/_seam.py:512` — same expression in `append_event`

## Analysis (pre-claim, evidence-backed)

All five are CodeQL taint over-approximations. No credential material reaches any log or
stdout at these sites.

**86/87 — the forced-write audit log.** The logged expression reads the `families` key of
`data["secret_override"]`, which is assigned two/three lines above from
`secret_screen.override_record(findings, reason)`. That helper returns
`{"reason", "families": sorted({f.family for f in findings}), "locations"}`. `f.family` is
a literal drawn from the module-level `SECRET_PATTERNS` table in `src/rebar/secret_screen.py`
— a fixed set of detector category names (e.g. "Anthropic API key", "GitHub token"). The
`SecretFinding` dataclass carries only `family`/`field`/`line` and **structurally has no
value field** — a documented, deliberate design property of that module ("Report the family
and the location, never the value"). CodeQL taints the whole `data` payload — correctly, it
may contain a credential shape, that is what the screen just detected — and cannot see that
this one key holds constant category names.

**83/84/85 — CLI usage errors.** CodeQL's sensitive-data heuristic flags
`_extract_allow_secret` on its NAME and taints its entire return tuple `(rest, reason)`,
so plain argv (`rest`) inherits the "secret" label. Two independent reasons this is false:
(1) the flag's value is the operator's free-text JUSTIFICATION for
`--allow-secret-pattern=<reason>`, not credential material; (2) the flag token is *stripped*
from `rest` before it is returned, so the flagged variable's value provably cannot reach any
of the three prints. What is actually printed is `argv[0]` (an unknown command name), an
unrecognised option token, and surplus positional arguments — the caller's own command line
echoed back on their own stderr in a usage error.

## Plan

1. Dismiss all 5 alerts via the code-scanning API with `dismissed_reason="false positive"`
   and a per-alert evidence comment, and record the same justification on this ticket.
2. Make no log-content change: redacting these would remove the diagnostic value
   (which detector was bypassed / which argument was rejected) for zero security gain.
3. Add regression tests that PIN the invariant so a future edit cannot start logging the
   value. Existing `tests/unit/test_secret_screen_e7a9.py::test_force_override_lands_the_write_and_records_it_as_forced`
   already pins the library forced-write route (asserts the value and its 12-char tail are
   absent from caplog). Extend coverage to the CLI route through
   `_commands.__init__.main` + `forced_secret_write` (`_seam.screen_event`, line 452), and
   assert the usage-error prints at 199/204/221 never carry the `--allow-secret-pattern`
   reason.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC1 — Each of the 5 alerts is dismissed via the code-scanning API with an
      evidence-backed false-positive justification, and the same per-alert justification is
      recorded as a comment on this ticket. No alert is dismissed without recorded evidence.
- [x] AC2 — Regression tests pin the invariant at both flagged routes: (a) driving the CLI
      forced-write path with a synthetic secret asserts the value and its 12-char head/tail
      fragments are absent from captured log records; (b) a test asserts the
      `--allow-secret-pattern` reason never appears in the usage-error output of
      `_commands.__init__.main`. Both are deterministic and use synthetic fixtures only.
- [x] AC3 — After the change lands, `gh api repos/navapbc/rebar/code-scanning/alerts` shows
      0 OPEN alerts for rule `py/clear-text-logging-sensitive-data` (all 5 dismissed).
- [x] AC4 — `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the touched test module pass; no production
      source behavior changes (tests-only change to `src/`-adjacent behavior: none).

## Testing

Run from inside the worktree with its venv first on `PATH`
(`env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH"`):

- `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_secret_screen_e7a9.py -q` — the new and existing
  regression tests pinning the no-secret-in-logs invariant at both flagged routes.
- `make lint` and `make typecheck` — the commit gate.
- `gh api repos/navapbc/rebar/code-scanning/alerts --jq '[.[] | select(.rule.id=="py/clear-text-logging-sensitive-data" and .state=="open")] | length'`
  — must print `0` after the dismissals, proving AC3.

This change is tests-only; there is no production behavior to roll back, and the alert
dismissals are reversible through the same code-scanning API (`-f state=open`).
